# Specification Quality Checklist: COGNITIVE Global Platform Upgrade

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-10-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.specify` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Notes

- Items marked `[x]` reflect the review performed at specification time. They certify requirements
  quality only — they do not certify that any requirement is implemented.
- SC-001 through SC-017 intentionally leave numeric performance thresholds unset. The source
  specifications make this normative: thresholds are set after a measured baseline exists. Each
  criterion therefore defines *what is measured* and *how it is verified*, which is what makes it
  verifiable without implementation detail. Reviewers who require pre-set numeric targets should
  raise that through `/speckit.clarify` rather than treating the omission as a defect.
- Named technologies, paths and third-party projects from the source specifications appear only in
  the Assumptions and Out-of-Scope sections as audit starting points. No requirement depends on a
  specific library, service or file path.
- The constitution file at `.specify/memory/constitution.md` is an unfilled template. Its semantic
  requirements are restated in FR-001–FR-017, and filling the constitution is tracked as a planning
  task, not assumed here.
- Next command: `/speckit.plan`.
